set.title: Two-step equations with integers · Unit Test

questions.question: On a balance, the left pan holds 3 identical x-bags together with 4 negative unit tiles, and the right pan holds 13 negative unit tiles. Which equation matches this balance?
questions.explain: Read each pan as a sum: 3 x-bags and 4 negative tiles give 3x − 4, and 13 negative tiles give −13. The common trap is reading negative unit tiles as +4, or flipping the sign of the x-bags, which are still positive.

questions.question: Solve for x: 3x − 6 = −21
questions.explain: Undo the subtraction first: add 6 to both sides to get 3x = −15, then divide both sides by 3 to get x = −5. The usual trap is subtracting 6 instead of adding it, which gives 3x = −27 and the wrong answer x = −9.

questions.question: Is x = −2 a solution of −5x + 3 = 13? Choose the correct check.
questions.explain: Substitute carefully: a negative times a negative is positive, so −5(−2) = 10, and 10 + 3 = 13 matches the right side. The most common trap is writing −5(−2) as −10 and concluding the solution fails.

questions.question: Which value of x makes 2(x + 6) = −10 true?
questions.explain: Divide both sides by 2 to get x + 6 = −5, then subtract 6 to get x = −11 (or distribute fully: 2x + 12 = −10). The classic trap is distributing to the x only, writing 2x + 6 = −10, which gives the wrong answer x = −8.

questions.question: At 5 p.m. the temperature at Sun Peaks is 4 °C, and it falls 3 °C every hour. Which equation finds the number of hours h until the temperature reaches −11 °C?
questions.explain: Start at 4 °C and take away 3 degrees per hour, so the temperature after h hours is 4 − 3h, and it must equal −11. The trap is writing 4 + 3h because the numbers 4 and 3 both look positive, but a falling temperature must be subtracted.

questions.question: Which value of m makes m/3 − 4 = −9 true?
questions.explain: Add 4 to both sides to get m/3 = −5, then multiply both sides by 3 to get m = −15. Two traps here: subtracting 4 instead of adding it (giving −39), and stopping at −5 without undoing the division by 3.

questions.question: Maya and Noah both solved 7 − 2x = −5. Maya says x = 6 and Noah says x = −6. Who is right, and why?
options: Both; the equation is true at 6 and −6
questions.explain: Subtract 7 from both sides to get −2x = −12, then divide by −2 (not 2), giving x = 6, and the check 7 − 12 = −5 confirms it. Noah kept the negative sign in the answer instead of cancelling it, and substituting −6 actually gives 7 + 12 = 19.

questions.question: On a winter evening in Kamloops the temperature is 6 °C at 6 p.m. It falls the same number of degrees each hour, and at 10 p.m. it is −6 °C. If it keeps falling at that rate, at what time will it reach −21 °C?
questions.explain: First find the rate: 6 − 4r = −6 gives 4r = 12, so r = 3 °C per hour; then 6 − 3h = −21 gives 3h = 27, so h = 9 hours after 6 p.m., which is 3 a.m. The big trap is a sign slip when moving the 6 across (using −21 + 6 = −15 instead of −21 − 6 = −27), or dividing 21 by 3 and forgetting the temperature started at 6 °C.
